private_note: I can't put any odds on where I'll land, and whatever we pick lasts a generation with no second chance. So I'm judging each plan by its worst case. Hazel's floor is 41, Birch's 36, Alder's 32, Today's 22 and Cedar's 15. Hazel's best case is lower, but I don't know my place well enough to bet on the top. If Hazel stalls, I'd move to Birch or Alder rather than let the convention fail and leave us with Today.
statement: None of us knows which fifth we'll go home to, and none of us can even guess the odds. The choice is permanent. Under those conditions I think the sensible question for each plan is how bad the worst case is. Under Hazel the worst-off households get 41 thousand, the highest floor any plan can sustain. That's nearly double what they get today, and the middle and fourth fifths still live reasonably well. Cedar raises the average, but it leaves whoever ends up at the bottom with 15 and no health coverage, and any one of us could be that household. Remember too that if no plan gets nine votes, we're stuck with Today, and its floor is 22. I'm ranking Hazel first, then Birch, then Alder. I'm open to joining a majority around any plan that protects the floor, and I ask the rest of you to think about where you would stand if your luck turned out bad.
